ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Dominant low-intensity (black/dark grey) base with localized high-intensity (white) circular regions; approximately 85:15 dark-to-light pixel ratio across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Symmetrical distribution of high-contrast white annular rings (rosettes) concentrated in the distal regions of both lobes, with a sparse distribution of individual white circular spots across the mid-section and a solid dark core surrounding the median notch.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped notch with an estimated internal angle of 42 degrees and a pixel-depth roughly equal to 15% of the total visible fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous boundary characterized by high-frequency, low-amplitude serrations; the left lobe trailing edge features two prominent, low-frequency large-scale indentations (notches) indicating significant tissue removal.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave upward sweep originating from the median notch, transitioning to a convex curve along the outer margins of the distal lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Widespread circular white ring clusters (barnacle scars) ranging from 15 to 45 pixels in diameter; highest spatial density observed on the outer 25% of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Low-contrast, light grey linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) detected on the lower right lobe, oriented approximately 25 degrees relative to the horizontal axis.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant scalloping and missing tissue segments on the left lobe trailing edge; dense colonization of barnacles (appearing as textured, high-contrast bulbous clusters) on the distal tips and leading edge margins.
other_distinctive_markers: Visible biological encrustation (barnacles) extending beyond the anatomical skin boundary at the extreme lateral tips of the fluke lobes.
